subject: Module sign-off: network bridge tests + telemetry plan
messages:
From: Jane Park <jane.park@acme.com>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: acme-sre <acme-sre@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Kickoff: network bridge sign-off and telemetry checklist

Thanks for the walkthrough this morning. Per our call, we want to capture a short sign-off checklist for the on-prem bridge (bare-metal aggregation switch -> private VPC) so our auditors can see:

- the final TF/Helm artifacts that will land in our CI pipeline
- a short test plan for bridge traffic and ACL verification
- the telemetry schema (what events/logs/metrics are sent to our Splunk instance)

We attached a one-page summary (acme-priv-bridge-test-plan.md) and included two sample outputs from our preflight diff in terraform-diff-acme-priv.txt. Could you confirm:

1) Which Terraform modules will be frozen for the release?
2) Who signs the module cert (Redwood or Acme SRE)?
3) Where will the post-deploy telemetry artifacts live (Drive link or S3)?

Thanks — we'd like to make the compliance handoff next Thurs (12/09).

— Jane
SRE Lead, Acme Corporation

[attachment: acme-priv-bridge-test-plan.md (text/markdown)]

From: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Jane Park <jane.park@acme.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: network bridge sign-off and telemetry checklist

Jane — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers inline, plus next actions below.

1) Terraform modules to freeze:
- priv-network (v1.8.2) — includes subnets, route targets, peering configs
- priv-bastion (v2.1.0) — bastion config referenced by Ops
- priv-egress (v1.0.4) — egress/egress-NAT rules

We'll pin those versions in the release branch and add module checksums to the artifact manifest.

2) Module sign-off: Redwood will provide the module build artifact and a checksum. Acme SRE will execute an independent checksum verification during the preflight. For the compliance record we can add a short signature line in the Drive doc; if Acme requires DocuSign we can route that as well.

3) Telemetry artifacts: we'll push to the shared Drive folder (link below) and create a one-time signed snapshot (s3://redwood-audits/acme/2026-12-09) for the auditors.

Next actions (owners):
- Marissa (Redwood) to publish the pinned TF tags + terraform-diff output to Drive (due 12/03)
- Kimberly (Redwood) to produce the helm-values-acme-priv.yaml with telemetry env flags (due 12/04)
- Acme SRE to run the bridge test plan and upload results (due 12/07)

I'll drop the Drive link here when Marissa confirms artifacts.

Cheers,
Dylan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

[inline attachment referenced: terraform-diff-acme-priv.txt]

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Jane Park <jane.park@acme.com>, acme-sre <acme-sre@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 08:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: network bridge sign-off and telemetry checklist

Uploading the artifacts now — preliminary Drive folder is up: https://drive.redwood.com/privdeploy/acme/bridge-test-plan

Files in folder:
- acme-priv-bridge-test-plan.md (authoritative test steps)
- terraform-diff-acme-priv.txt (plan output, redacted creds)
- module-manifest-20261202.txt (module names + pinned tags + checksums)

A couple of notes from the TF plan:
- priv-network will require an additional lifecycle ignore for the vlan resource until the hardware team completes the NIC firmware update (we call that out in the manifest).
- Helm values include a telemetry toggle: REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_MODE: external-forward. Kimberly will add the Splunk endpoint and cert thumbprint in the values file.

I'll attach the module-manifest once the CI build produces checksums (expected EOD PST).

— Marissa
Program Manager, Private Deployments

[attachment: module-manifest-20261202.txt]

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jane Park <jane.park@acme.com>, dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 14:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: network bridge sign-off and telemetry checklist

Hi all — pushed helm-values-acme-priv.yaml to the Drive folder. Key excerpts:

- telemetry.enabled: true
- telemetry.forwarder.type: splunk-hec
- telemetry.splunk_hec.url: https://splunk.acme.internal:8088
- telemetry.splunk_hec.token_hash: <sha256 placeholder>
- telemetry.event_schema: [connection_open, conn_bytes, acl_denied, route_mismatch, cfg_change]

Testing plan for telemetry:
1) smoke: health ping every 10s (verify point-in-time ingestion)
2) ACL exercise: trigger a controlled deny and confirm acl_denied events within 30s
3) drift: apply a no-op terraform with changed tag values to ensure cfg_change events are emitted

Also flagging an ops item: we need an agreed TTL for audit artifacts. Proposal: 365 days in S3 then move to Glacier Deep (unless Acme requests longer).

Kimberly
Security & Compliance Engineer, Redwood Inference

[attachment: helm-values-acme-priv.yaml]

From: acme-sre <acme-sre@acme.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jane Park <jane.park@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Dec 2026 10:14:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: network bridge sign-off and telemetry checklist

Thanks — completed the smoke and ACL exercise earlier. Quick summary:
- smoke: health ping received and parsed by Splunk within 6s
- ACL exercise: acl_denied events generated; however in ~5% of trials the src_ip field was missing.
- terraform plan diff aligns with our expectation except for one extra route in priv-egress that we didn't request.

We uploaded logs and a small sample of events to the Drive folder: /results/acl-sample.log, /results/smoke-20261206.json.

Requests before sign-off:
1) Can Redwood add a short telemetry validation script in the helm chart (python script that checks required fields and exits non-zero if missing)?
2) Remove the unwanted route in priv-egress or add an explicit explicit lifecycle ignore until we reconcile with the hardware team.
3) Confirm audit TTL policy and whether Acme can request an extension on a per-case basis.

— Acme SRE

[attachments: /results/acl-sample.log (text), /results/smoke-20261206.json (application/json)]

From: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: acme-sre <acme-sre@acme.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, jane.park <jane.park@acme.com>, hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Dec 2026 16:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: network bridge sign-off and telemetry checklist

Great validation — really helpful. Quick responses and plan: 

1) Telemetry validation: Kimberly and I will add a small post-install hook (preflight) in the Helm chart that calls a Python validator against the Splunk HEC endpoint. Target: PR by 12/08. If it fails the hook will mark the release as failed in CI and attach the event sample.

2) priv-egress route: Marissa flagged this earlier — we'll add an explicit lifecycle ignore and a comment in the module-manifest so auditors can see the intentional exception, then engage the hardware team for firmware reconciliation. Expect a clean manifest update by EOD 12/07.

3) Audit TTL: default 365 days into S3, with a documented request process for extensions (via Support ticket). Hannah — can you own the extension flow and the small doc that explains retention + request SLA?

If no blockers from Acme after the minor fixes above we'll schedule the compliance handoff on 12/09 and produce the signed artifact snapshot at s3://redwood-audits/acme/2026-12-09.

Thanks everyone — I'll open the three follow-up PRs and link them in the Drive folder when ready.

Dylan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
